fact_check.claim: Many riders stop at the first snow, but some keep going
fact_check.note: Source: many cyclists 'put a hold on their cycling at the first sign of snow,' some keep riding in severe conditions. Dated 2007.

fact_check.claim: Ithaca and Cornell's campus pose challenges to bikers because of cold climate and hilly terrain
fact_check.note: Source: 'Between its cold climate and hilly terrain, Ithaca and Cornell's campus pose challenges to bikers.'

fact_check.claim: In 2007 riders told the Sun that plowed snow and pothole covers in bike lanes can push cyclists out into traffic
fact_check.note: Source says riders sometimes 'have to swerve out of the bike lane to avoid danger' because of plowed snow and pothole covers. 'Into traffic' is not in the source.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's snow page does not say bike lanes get special treatment
fact_check.note: Page does not mention bike lanes.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's bicycle specialist recommended a second bike for winter because salt, snow and ice wear down a year-round bike
fact_check.note: Lois Chaplin, bicycle and pedestrian specialist, recommends a separate winter bike; wear from 'snow, ice and salt.'

fact_check.claim: Wash and lubricate the chain after every ride once roads are salted
fact_check.note: Source says clean and lubricate bikes after each ride, especially once roads are salted. Source says 'bikes', article narrows to 'chain'; acceptable.

fact_check.claim: Few people bike to campus even in mild weather; numbers fall further with snow and ice, per the same article
fact_check.note: Source gives a Transportation Services survey: 71% of undergraduates walk, 1.4% bike. Snow drop-off supported by 'hold on cycling at first snow'. Figures are 2007 and could be added with a date.

fact_check.claim: Grounds covers about 15 miles of roads, 61 miles of walkways, 114 acres of parking lots
fact_check.note: Page lists '15 Miles of Roads, 61 Miles of Walkways, 114 Acres of Parking Lots.'

fact_check.claim: Report slippery spots on campus at 607-255-5322
fact_check.note: Page directs to Customer Service/EMCS at 607-255-5322 for slippery conditions.

fact_check.claim: City requires residents, businesses and owners to keep sidewalks free of snow and ice; city may clear and bill the owner
fact_check.note: Source cites City Code Chapter 178-3; city may clear and charge if not done within 'the required timeframe' (not stated).

fact_check.claim: Cornell requires you to stay off sidewalks and pathways unless they are marked shared
fact_check.note: Source says only 'Bicycles, like other vehicles, belong on streets not on sidewalks.' It has no exception for marked shared paths, and does not mention pathways. The following sentence ('you cannot simply hop onto an uncleared-street alternative') is also unsupported and unclear.

fact_check.claim: Bikes have the same road rights and duties as other vehicles
fact_check.note: Source: 'Bicycles have the same rights to the road as other vehicles' and must follow the same traffic laws.

fact_check.claim: Must use legal headlights and taillights at dusk or night
fact_check.note: Page: 'legal headlights and taillights if you ever ride at dusk or at night.'

fact_check.claim: Bell or horn required; a personal strobe is not a legal taillight
fact_check.note: Both stated on the page.

fact_check.claim: Registering a bike is free; Cornell asks you to register with it and your local municipality
fact_check.note: Page: 'free of charge'; register with Cornell Commuter & Parking Services and the local municipality.

fact_check.claim: Bikes locked to railings, signposts or trees may be impounded
fact_check.note: Listed among impound reasons.

fact_check.claim: Cornell has over 1,000 bike parking stations
fact_check.note: Page: 'over 1,000 bike parking stations across campus.'

fact_check.claim: About seven miles of bike lanes and two miles of shared paths on campus
fact_check.note: Guest column: 'approximately seven miles of bike lanes, and two miles of shared paths on campus.' A student guest column, not an official source; ideally link an official Cornell page.

fact_check.claim: Every TCAT bus has a front-mounted bike rack at no extra fare
fact_check.note: Stated on page.

fact_check.claim: Bike Walk Tompkins keeps a list of local bike shops
fact_check.note: Page says the nonprofit maintains a local resources list with a 'Local Bike Shops' section linking to it. Better to link Bike Walk Tompkins' own page.

fact_check.claim: One rider said good brakes matter more than anything for stopping
fact_check.note: Wine: braking matters most; 'If you have good brakes, your stopping distance isn't too affected by weather conditions.' Paraphrase is slightly stronger than the quote.

fact_check.claim: Hat or headband under helmet, eye protection, synthetic or wool layers, no cotton, ski clothing works
fact_check.note: All in Chaplin's advice.

fact_check.claim: The 2007 article's cyclist stops biking below 40°F
fact_check.note: Chaplin stops when it drops 'below 40 degrees.' The article attributes it to 'the cyclist'; name her (Cornell's bicycle specialist).

fact_check.claim: First-year degree students get unlimited TCAT rides
fact_check.note: Automatic OmniRide privileges; expire Aug 31 for fall entrants, Dec 31 for spring entrants.

fact_check.claim: Other registered students ride free after 6 p.m. weekdays and all weekend
fact_check.note: Source ties this to registered degree-program students (a year or more) who stay registered; 'other registered students' drops that condition. Page also says PhD students and graduate assistants get free OmniRide passes, which the article omits.

fact_check.claim: OmniRide annual pass is $200 per year
fact_check.note: $200 per year, pro-rated monthly, expires Aug 31 of the following year.

fact_check.claim: Cash fare, no pass: $1.50
fact_check.note: Page mentions $1.50 only as a fallback: 'If your CU ID card isn't accepted, you may need to pay the $1.50 fare with cash.' It is not presented as the general no-pass fare. Link TCAT's own fare page instead.

fact_check.claim: Ithaca Bikeshare: $1.50 to unlock plus $0.25 per minute, $25 day pass, $60 monthly plan
fact_check.note: Pay as You Go $1.50 + $0.25/min plus tax; day pass $25 (2 hrs); monthly $60 (30 min/day). Page also lists a $1.50 convenience fee for trips not ending in a hub, which is omitted.

fact_check.claim: Class 1 pedal-assist e-bikes, riders must be 16 or older
fact_check.note: Confirmed; under-18 riders need a parent or guardian's consent.

fact_check.claim: The Sun's 2023 article quotes a student saying it was too snowy for bikeshare, and its per-minute rate was lower
fact_check.note: Student said 'It's just a little too snowy at the moment.' Article printed 15 cents per minute plus $1 unlock, so current prices are higher.

fact_check.claim: Bikeshare page does not say whether service pauses in winter; email help@ithacabikeshare.org
fact_check.note: No winter statement found. help@ithacabikeshare.org appears as the main contact, though one page link points to support@goithaca.org.

fact_check.claim: By late afternoon in December it is dark
fact_check.note: No source cited for the daylight claim. Cornell page only says lights are required at dusk or night. Add a sunset time with a source (e.g. timeanddate.com Ithaca) or soften.

beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2007 Sun feature with gear tips and no current rules, costs, snow-clearing info or TCAT backup plan; our page answers the question in the first paragraph and adds current Cornell rules, bus costs and bikeshare prices. It loses ground only where it repeats the 2007 advice without its numbers and where a few facts are wrong.
changes: Fix the sourced facts that currently mismatch (sidewalk rule, TCAT fare conditions) so a student acting on the page is not misled.

Give the 2007 survey figures with the year (71% of undergraduates walk, 1.4% bike to campus) in place of the vague 'a minority of riders', and name Lois Chaplin, Cornell's bicycle and pedestrian specialist, as the source of the 40°F rule.
Add one concrete winter daylight fact with a source (sunset time in Ithaca in December) so the lights advice has a number.

fixes: In the bullet 'Plowed snow in the bike lane', change 'can push cyclists out into traffic' to say riders told the Sun they sometimes have to swerve out of the bike lane to avoid danger because of plowed snow and pothole covers; source https://cornellsun.com/2007/11/12/cyclists-persevere-through-wintry-weather

In the paragraph beginning 'Cornell also requires you to stay off sidewalks', remove 'and pathways unless they are marked shared' and delete the sentence 'In winter that means you cannot simply hop onto an uncleared-street alternative.' Say only that Cornell says bicycles belong on streets, not sidewalks, and have the same rights to the road as other vehicles; source https://sustainable.cornell.edu/news/rules-road-biking-season

In the TCAT cost_table and the paragraph below it, change 'Other registered students' to the condition on the source page (registered degree-program students who stay registered ride free after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day weekends), and add that PhD students and graduate assistants get free OmniRide passes; source https://fcs.cornell.edu/departments/transportation-delivery-services/sustainable-transportation-options/bus-services-privileges-passes

Replace the table row 'Cash fare, no pass: $1.50' and the matching sentence, because the Cornell page gives $1.50 only as the cash fare if your CU ID card is not accepted. Either relabel it 'Cash fare if your CU ID is not accepted: $1.50' with that Cornell link, or drop it and link TCAT's own fare page (tcatbus.com) after opening it to confirm the general fare.

In the first paragraph, replace 'a minority of Cornell riders do' with the dated figure from the 2007 Sun article: a Transportation Services survey then found 1.4% of undergraduates biked to campus and 71% walked; source https://cornellsun.com/2007/11/12/cyclists-persevere-through-wintry-weather

In 'When to give up and take TCAT', change 'The 2007 article's cyclist' to 'Lois Chaplin, Cornell's bicycle and pedestrian specialist, told the Sun in 2007 that she stops biking when the temperature drops below 40 degrees'.
In 'What you are required to have', replace 'By late afternoon in December it is dark' with a sourced Ithaca December sunset time and link, or delete the sentence.
In the Ithaca Bikeshare paragraph, add that trips that do not end in a hub carry a $1.50 convenience fee; source https://ithacabikeshare.org

Replace the sustainable.cornell.edu biking page link used for 'Bike Walk Tompkins keeps a list of local shops' with Bike Walk Tompkins' own bike shop page, or reword to 'Cornell's biking page links to a Bike Walk Tompkins list of local shops'.
